problem: Large VLN models are too heavy for edge deployment, and existing VLN distillation (representation, attention, logit) depends on teacher quality and does not separate local cues for immediate action from global cues for long-term planning.
motivation: Navigation errors compound over time, so a weak teacher caps the student. An explicit, compact evidence interface between teacher and student (a small set of navigable queries) could be both a compression bottleneck and a distillation target.
key_idea: Build a DUET-style teacher whose cross-modal reasoning runs on a few learnable local/global navigable query slots, then distill those query slots with slot-adaptive weighting plus policy KL into a much shallower student.
insight: The query slots serve as a compact, structured interface that is easier to transfer than generic attention/feature/logit KD. On R2R, the QAD student beats an Attn+Feat+Logit KD baseline by 3.00 SPL (69.54 vs 66.54), and removing NTD while keeping policy KL drops SPL from 69.54 to 61.44. Separate local and global banks beat shared generic queries (R2R SPL 71.98 vs 69.21), and distilling both branches beats either alone (SR 79.12 vs 75.41 global-only and 74.22 local-only). Token-adaptive weighting also beats uniform weights (SR 77.52 vs 79.12).
method: Navigable Query Generator (NQG): learnable local (K_L=32) and global (K_G=32) query slots cross-attend to current-view candidate tokens and the topological-graph node tokens, followed by an FFN residual, giving per-step navigable queries.

Instruction-Query Aligner (IQA): concatenates local and global queries, applies self-attention and FFN, then cross-attends to instruction tokens (queries=navigable tokens) to yield the fused state for the policy head.

Navigation-aware Token-adaptive Distillation (NTD): L2 loss between teacher and student query slots of the same index, weighted per slot by 1-sigmoid(diagonal cosine similarity) and normalized per branch, so poorly aligned slots get larger weights; used in both pretraining and fine-tuning.
Policy KL distillation: KL between teacher and student action distributions during fine-tuning; L_D = alpha*L_NTD + (1-alpha)*L_pi with alpha=0.5.
Compact student: same topology, but text/pano encoder layers 6/2 -> 1/1, NQG blocks 4 -> 1, IQA layers 3 -> 1; params 150.78M -> 9.56M, GFLOPs 45.56 -> 1.92.

Two-stage training: train the teacher to convergence, freeze it, then train the student with distillation in both pretraining (MLM, SAP, OG) and fine-tuning; CLIP-B/16 features, METER init, EnvEdit and synthetic data augmentation.

setting.backbone: DUET-style dual-scale transformer with query bottleneck; teacher 150.78M, student 9.56M (both trained; CLIP-B/16 features, METER init)
setting.training_data: R2R/RxR/REVERIE/SOON train sets plus the synthetic extended datasets used by prior work (e.g., ScaleVLN-style), EnvEdit feature augmentation, speaker pseudo-labels with environmental dropout; MLM+SAP(+OG) pretraining
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (CLIP-B/16 features) plus instruction text and topological graph
setting.privileged: none (Jetson Nano used only for runtime benchmarking, not navigation)

results: The student (9.56M params, 1.92 GFLOPs) reaches R2R test-unseen SR 79.12/SPL 69.54, close to the teacher's 80.43/71.98 and above MiniVLN's 77.59/68.05. Its parameters are 93.65% fewer than the teacher's, and it runs at 51.6 steps/s on Jetson Nano against 15.9 for GOAT. The teacher also beats GOAT and MAGIC-L on all four benchmarks.
limitations: Sim-only evaluation on pre-extracted panoramic features and graph navigation; no physical-robot navigation, and sim-to-real remains open.
The student still fails at fine-grained landmark and room grounding and at precise STOP calibration.
Diagonal slot-index matching assumes teacher and student share the same query-slot design; the best slot count may not transfer to other architectures.
